# Reflect on your own skills and development as a writer

- What are the areas you think you are good at? Where can you improve?
Good- Keeping it concise, using logical flow in writing
Improve- certain aspects of grammar e.g. Affect vs Effect or species name conventions, habit of word fluff to reach word count

- How will you further develop your skills over the coming year? Can you make a specific, detailed plan?
Write in assignments for the upcoming year, proofread, make chnges and understand why changes need to be made
# Reflect on writing more generally

- What principles of composition discussed today did you find most useful?
Omit needless words (i write consicely but then add needless words in to reach the word count)
- If you were going to formulate your own writing rules, what would they be?

# Commit your reflections to writing
Compose a paragraph summarizing your reflections. Remember to use the "commit" process to save your changes when you are finished.
I am good at keeping my writing concise and ensuring my ideas follow a clear, logical structure, but I need to improve my grammar and avoid adding unnecessary words just to meet word counts. Over the coming year, I will develop my writing by carefully proofreading assignments, making corrections, and understanding why each change improves the quality of my work. My main writing rules would be to omit needless words, maintain a logical flow, and prioritise clarity and accuracy over reaching a word count.
